definitions.meaning: a band worn on the finger, or a circular strip round something
the clear resonant note of a bell

explanation.surface: A remark about the crisp tone of a musical group.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedding band is a circlet for the finger, and a bell's peal is its clear note: two senses of one word.

clue.text: Young reporter on a Caribbean island

parts.note: a cub is a young animal, and in newspaper slang a cub reporter is a novice

explanation.surface: A novice journalist is sent to cover a story on a Caribbean island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Young reporter' is a cub reporter; only CUB is wanted, and in a down clue 'on' puts it above A.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest island of the Greater Antilles lies in the Caribbean Sea.

parts.note: men means people in the general sense

indicators.note: initially says to take only the opening letter of the word drugs

explanation.surface: Patients on medication start to get better.
explanation.definitionFit: To repair or put right is to make better, a plain synonym.

indicators.note: changes tells us the letters of the two words before it are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A knight is told to wear his whole suit of armour as it is, without alteration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apply no changes' reads as an instruction, but 'changes' is the signal to rearrange APPLY and NO.
explanation.definitionFit: The word originally meant a complete suit of armour, later any full splendid array.

parts.note: a spell is a period of time, a season of something
a bound is a leap or spring

explanation.surface: Someone is enchanted by the coming of springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'season-spring' looks like springtime; it is two separate synonyms joined.
explanation.definitionFit: Held as if by magic, fascinated, is the sense of being under a charm.

clue.text: What crosses face is very little help

parts.note: minute means tiny or very little
a hand is help, as in lend a hand

explanation.surface: Someone protests that the assistance they got was negligible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'face' is a clock face, which the long pointer sweeps across once an hour.
explanation.definitionFit: On a clock the longer pointer travels round the dial, passing over its face every hour.

clue.text: Evil glare from one who won't come clean?

definitions.meaning: someone who refuses to wash looks grubby, read literally

explanation.surface: A guilty person who won't confess gives a nasty stare.
explanation.definitionFit: A scowl of contempt is the idiom, and an unwashed person literally appears grimy.

clue.text: Look amazed at back of big animal

indicators.note: back of says to take the final letter of the word big

parts.note: an ape is an animal

explanation.surface: Someone stares in wonder at the hindquarters of a large beast.
explanation.definitionFit: To stare open-mouthed in astonishment is the plain sense.

clue.text: Source of rumour that may bear fruit

definitions.meaning: word of mouth, the informal channel by which gossip spreads

explanation.surface: A piece of gossip that might pay off.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for an unofficial channel of gossip, and literally a plant on which grapes grow.

clue.text: Make splendid progress on European trip

parts.note: grand means splendid or magnificent
a tour, like a royal progress, is a journey from place to place

explanation.surface: A traveller makes fine headway on a journey through Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Young aristocrats of the 17th and 18th centuries took a long cultural journey through the continent.

indicators.note: we hear says the word for nobody is taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: none means nobody

explanation.surface: A claim that not a single person is devout.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious, as a noun, is a member of a holy order, such as a sister in a convent.

indicators.note: turning says the entry's letters are read backwards

parts.note: 16 stands for the answer to 16 across, the Mediterranean island where Napoleon was exiled

explanation.surface: Someone reaching sixteen is now healthy and capable.
explanation.walkthrough: '16' looks like an age but is a cross-reference to the island at 16 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Fit in the sense of capable or competent, as in fit for the job.

definitions.meaning: a gratuity, a small sum given to a waiter

explanation.surface: A small present consisting of counsel.
explanation.definitionFit: A gratuity left for service, and a useful hint: two senses of one word.

definitions.meaning: a sweetened whipped cream named after a French town
a delicate bobbin lace made in the same town

explanation.surface: A question whether a lace is of the cream-coloured kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweetened whipped cream and a fine silk bobbin lace both take the name of a town north of Paris.

clue.text: Estimate roughly 24 hours to finish work

parts.note: to call it is to give a rough figure, as in call it ten pounds
a day lasts 24 hours

explanation.surface: Someone guesses the job will take about a day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' looks like an anagram signal but belongs with 'Estimate'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to stop working for now and go home.

indicators.note: breaking says one piece splits the other and sits inside it

parts.note: absent means away
an orb is a ball or sphere

explanation.surface: A footballer picks up the ball and makes a breakaway.
explanation.definitionFit: Soaking up liquid, as a sponge does, is to take it up.

clue.text: Sort of sketch in thin album, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters of the words before it could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A small drawing tucked inside a slim scrapbook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' signals an anagram of THIN and ALBUM; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief rough drawing, small enough to be the size of a fingertip.

indicators.note: out suggests the word Bale is put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone parachutes from an aircraft away from an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bale out' reads as an escape by parachute; 'out' is the anagram signal on BALE.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mediterranean isle off Tuscany, Napoleon's first place of exile.

indicators.note: entwined says the letters of couples are twisted together into a new order

explanation.surface: A photographer gets a near shot of lovers in an embrace.
explanation.definitionFit: A photograph or film shot taken from very near, showing fine detail.

parts.note: to cop is slang for to get or acquire
IOUs, notes reading I owe you, are written by debtors

explanation.surface: Someone collects a pile of promissory notes from people who owe money.
explanation.definitionFit: Abundant, in great quantity, is a straight synonym.

definitions.meaning: a peak, here one built by eruption
something that might explode, read literally

explanation.surface: A climber thinks a peak could be scaled.
explanation.definitionFit: A cone-shaped peak formed by lava, which may erupt or blow up at any time.

definitions.meaning: a pillar holding up a bridge or arch
a structure jutting into the sea with amusements on it, a feature of British seaside resorts

explanation.surface: Backing for a show at a beach resort.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillar holding up a bridge span, and the promenade platform with arcades at a British resort.

parts.note: to block is to obstruct
a head is a principal, as of a school

explanation.surface: A dim headteacher gets in the way.
explanation.definitionFit: A dunce or stupid person, someone with a wooden skull.

definitions.meaning: the joint between the thigh and the pelvis
the red fruit of the wild rose

explanation.surface: A body part that yields fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The ball-and-socket joint at the top of the leg, and the red berry of the wild rose.

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: Someone resides on the northern side of a peak.
explanation.walkthrough: BEN is a Scottish word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis.
explanation.definitionFit: Scottish mountains bear this word as a prefix, such as Ben Nevis.

indicators.note: listening to says the word for poems counts by its sound

parts.note: lays are narrative poems or songs

explanation.surface: Someone unwinds by hearing verse.
explanation.definitionFit: To idle or lounge about is to take it easy.

parts.note: AC is the abbreviation for account, which is a bill
a company is a society or fellowship

explanation.surface: A man called Bill escorts a member of high society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name; it is an account, abbreviated AC.
explanation.definitionFit: To go along with someone, as a chaperone does.

clue.text: A wet way to defend castle

definitions.text: A wet way to defend castle

parts.words: A wet way to defend castle
parts.note: a water-filled ditch around a fortress keeps attackers out

explanation.surface: A soggy method of holding a fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep trench filled with water was dug round a fortification to protect it.

parts.note: shy means timid or nervous

explanation.surface: A grey horse that is jumpy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grey' looks like a horse; it is the definition, meaning ash-coloured.
explanation.definitionFit: Pale grey like the powder left by a fire, a colour word.

parts.note: the word for spun fibre also means a long rambling story

explanation.surface: A question about the plot line of a story.
explanation.definitionFit: Spun thread is used for knitting, and a long story is spun out the same way.

definitions.meaning: an upright spar, as on a ship
beech nuts and acorns fallen to the forest floor, eaten by pigs

explanation.surface: A post supplies fodder for swine.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's upright spar, and fallen forest nuts eaten by swine: two meanings.

clue.text: Where Rachel and Sian may come from?

definitions.text: Where Rachel and Sian may come from?

indicators.note: come from hints that the county's letters derive from the two names rearranged

explanation.surface: Wondering which region two women are natives of.
explanation.walkthrough: LANCASHIRE is a county in north-west England; the two names rearranged give it.
explanation.definitionFit: A county in north-west England, a home region for anyone born there.
